page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 8 physical CPU cores with hyperthreading, providing 16 virtual CPUs alongside 35 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates instruction set extensions including AVX, AVX-512, AES, FMA, and BMI2. The instance is provisioned with 128.0 GB of system memory, delivering a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio without integrated GPU accelerators or local storage disks. Network performance is constrained to a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps under KVM virtualization.

Benchmark evaluation reveals a clear trade-off between single-threaded execution and multi-core throughput. Single-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng single-core tests and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into lower performance tiers due to moderate processor clock rates. Conversely, multi-threaded workloads leverage all 16 vCPUs to achieve average performance across multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 decompression tests. Memory bandwidth tests indicate typical middle-tier performance for cached and uncached operations.

Given its high memory-to-core capacity and moderate multi-threaded performance, the ecs.se1.4xlarge provides a balanced environment for memory-intensive applications that do not demand high single-core clock speeds. Database operations, Redis key-value caching achieving 11.3 million SET operations per second, static web serving at 7.83 GB/s, and software compilation tasks perform within expected mid-range limits. The instance delivers solid resource density for large-footprint tasks, offering cost efficiency for memory-heavy enterprise deployments that rely on external block storage.

Benchmark data demonstrates a key trade-off: single-core CPU execution ranks in lower performance tiers due to moderate clock frequencies, whereas multi-core throughput, software compilation, and memory bandwidth achieve average mid-range scores.
